name: The Person Who Knew Where Everything Was
habitat: Second desk from the window, any office in Britain.
card: Appeared on no organisation chart. Knew which drawer, which form, which Brenda. Could not be replaced, and for the same reason was never promoted.
got: Being needed twelve times a day.
miss: Being needed twelve times a day.
status: Critically endangered. A search box now knows where everything is. It does not know which Brenda.

name: The Out-of-Office Reply
habitat: Inboxes, Fridays, the whole of August.
card: The one lie everybody agreed to. "I will have limited access to email" meant "I am on a beach with unlimited access to email and I am choosing you last."
miss: Writing it at 5.58 on the last day with a taxi outside.
status: Extinct. Your assistant answers for you now, in your voice, from the beach.

name: The Cover Letter
card: A page in which a grown adult explained their lifelong passion for regional logistics. For its final years it was written by one machine and read by another, and neither was moved.
got: Nothing. This is the only exhibit in the museum with no mourners.
status: Dead. Please do not leave flowers.

name: The Work Experience Kid
habitat: Beside the photocopier, in a tie that belonged to an uncle.
card: Did the copying. Was shown the stationery cupboard. Learned, by Thursday, how adults talk when the boss has left. That last part was the education.
got: A first look at what a job is actually like, which is mostly waiting.
status: Endangered. There is no copying left to do, and nobody has worked out where the other thing gets learned.

name: The Meeting That Could Have Been an Email
card: It is an email now. One machine writes it and another sums it up for people who will not read the summary.
got: A biscuit, a seat, and an hour in which nothing could be asked of you.
miss: "Shall we give it two more minutes for people to join?"
status: Survives as a habit. Six people still turn up, for the company.

name: The Reference
card: A letter in which one employer told another absolutely nothing, with great care. "He was always punctual" could end a career. "We wish her well" could end two.
got: For the writer, revenge. For the reader, a puzzle.
status: Dying. The new employer has already read everything you ever wrote.

name: The Junior
habitat: The worst desk. Later, a slightly better desk.
card: Did the dull part of the job, badly at first. By doing it, learned the rest. Everyone senior in the building was once this exhibit and has forgotten.
got: Somebody to ask. Somebody to blame. Eventually, somebody to be.
status: Vanishing, and the museum is worried. Nobody has said where next year's seniors are supposed to come from.

name: The Expense Claim
card: The last great amateur form of fiction. A sandwich became "client hospitality". A taxi home became "travel between sites".
got: A small, private win against the firm.
status: Extinct. The machine has seen the receipt, the map and the sandwich.

name: The Typing Pool
card: Killed by an earlier machine. Kept here as a warning to the other exhibits, none of whom think it applies to them.
got: A wage, a friend, a bus home with the others.
status: Extinct. On permanent loan from the last time.

name: The Tea Round
card: A system of debts more complicated than any bank. Everyone knows who owes whom, nobody writes it down, and one man in accounts has not made a cup since 2019.
got: A reason to stand up, and the only reliable news in the building.
status: Thriving. Not yet in the collection. No machine has found a way to owe somebody a tea.
